title_he: הַלְלוּהוּ וְעִבְדוּהוּ, כִּי הוּא הָאָדוֹן הַגָּדוֹל
review: The hymn is the incarnation as worship: 1:1–4 is Ps 148:2 (כָּל־מַלְאָכָיו … כָּל־צְבָאָיו) with Isa 6:2–3, 2:1–4 1 John 4:9–10 with Isa 7:14 (עִמָּנוּאֵל), 3:1–4 2 Cor 8:9 with Phil 2:8, 4:1–4 Luke 2:7,12 with John 1:29 and 2 Cor 1:20, and 5:1–4 Rom 11:33.

2:1 מָה רַבָּה הִיא הָאַהֲבָה — the Arabic يَا لَهُ حُبًّا عَظِيمًا is an exclamation ('O what a great love!'); biblical Hebrew cannot put an abstract noun in the vocative, so the line turns it into the psalm's rhetorical question-form (Ps 31:20, מָה רַב־טוּבְךָ), which is the same exclamation in Hebrew idiom.

2:4 וְעִמָּנוּאֵל שְׁמוֹ — the Hebrew keeps the name untranslated, as Isa 7:14 and Matt 1:23 do, and it is the stanza's point that the name is a sentence: the Arabic ends the line with the name alone, and so does the Hebrew.

3:3 שִׁפְלוּת לֹא תֶּחָקֵר הִיא — the Arabic بِاتِّضَاعٍ لَيْسَ يُوصَف is 'with a meekness that cannot be described'; the Hebrew uses the Niphal of חָקַר, the verb of Job 5:9 and Isa 40:28 for what cannot be searched out, so the line says the lowliness is unsearchable rather than merely unmentioned.

5:3 לֹא יַשִּׂיגֵהוּ הַשֵּׂכֶל — the Arabic لَا يَسُوغُ الْبَحْثُ فِيهِ is literally 'searching in it is not permitted'; the Hebrew shifts from permission to capacity (the mind does not reach it), because a Hebrew line forbidding investigation of the mystery would contradict the stanza's own invitation to receive it.
